newsitem.title: FINLAND: VALMET, RAUTARUUKKI SET STEEL J/V.
newsitem.headline: VALMET, RAUTARUUKKI SET STEEL J/V.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Valmet Oy said in a statement on Thursday it will set up a steel processing joint venture, PreSteel Oy, with Finnish steel group Rautaruukki Oy.
Rautaruukki will own 55 percent and Valmet 45 percent of the new company, Valmet said.
"Valmet and Rautaruukki are setting up a joint venture company ... for the prefabrication of hot-rolled plates," Valmet said. PreSteel will produce roll blanks for Valmet.

"Rautaruukki aims to increase its operations of prefabrication of steel plates produced at the Raahe steel works by expanding the product range and so obtain new customers," it said. Raahe is an industrial town in north-western Finland.

For itself, Valmet said it would "focus on its own core business; manufacturing of paper and board machines." Valmet also aimed at raising the effectiveness of its main material suppliers and subcontractors, it said.
Rautaruukki released its own similarily phrased statement.
PreSteel was scheduled to start production in the autumn of 1997, Valmet and Rautaruukki said.
